# E13 — the engine section's numbers, finalised

The work order asked for a finished table: eight processes, each with what it
solves, where it was validated, its measured numbers and its limits, every figure
traceable to a file under `runs/`, and no new experiments.

**That table already existed** — `engine-rig/ENGINE_TABLE.md`, generated by
`tools/engine_table.py` from probes into artifacts, hand-edits forbidden, drift
guarded by `tests/test_engine_table.py`. So this item is not a second table. It
is the audit that the first one's numbers say what the artifacts say.

They did not, in two ways, and the second one was live in the published file.

## 1 · Three numbers in the paper's table were never numbers

Rows 2 and 3 of the committed `ENGINE_TABLE.md` read, verbatim:

```
| 2 | `cegis_miner` | … | Fixture A ({cegis.fixtureA_transitions} transitions); 193 `gridworld` worlds …
| 3 | `zero_space`  | … | Fixture B `pair_flip` ({zs.fixtureB_features} features); 200 `parityworld` …
                       … one resting on Fixture B's {zs.fixtureB_transitions} are indistinguishable …
```

Three `{fact.key}` placeholders, published as text, in the table the paper's
engine section is built from.

**Why nothing caught it.** `_PLACEHOLDER` was `re.compile(r"\{([a-z0-9_.]+)\}")`.
Of the 174 fact keys, exactly three carry a capital letter —
`cegis.fixtureA_transitions`, `zs.fixtureB_features`, `zs.fixtureB_transitions` —
so the matcher never saw them. Four independent guards were in place and all four
were blind for the same reason:

* `sub()`'s own unknown-key check (`raise ProbeError(f"table references unknown
  fact {key!r}")`) is inside the substitution callback. It can only fire for keys
  the pattern already matched, so it could not fire for these. Its docstring —
  *"An unknown key raises rather than leaving a silent gap in the table"* — states
  the exact guarantee that was not held.
* `--check` renders the table and compares it to the committed file. Both sides
  contain the same unsubstituted placeholder, so they match: it printed
  `174 facts verified; ENGINE_TABLE.md is current`.
* `verify()` *did* probe all three facts against their artifacts, correctly, every
  run. The values were right and available (49, 16, 40). Only the rendering
  dropped them, and nothing compared the rendered cell to the verified value.
* `tests/test_engine_table.py::test_every_number_in_the_table_is_backed_by_a_probe`
  blanks placeholders before hunting for bare numerals — using **its own second
  copy** of the same `[a-z0-9_.]+` pattern. An unexpanded key contributes no
  digits, so it produced no offender either way. Two copies of one regex had
  drifted into agreeing on the same mistake.

**Fixed** by widening the class *and* by not trusting it: `sub()` now re-reads its
own output with `_ANY_BRACE = re.compile(r"\{[^{}]*\}")`, a deliberately dumber
matcher that knows nothing about what a fact key looks like, and raises if
anything brace-wrapped survives. Widening the class fixes today's three keys; the
second guard is what catches the next key that falls outside whatever the class
becomes. The test file now imports `engine_table._PLACEHOLDER` instead of keeping
a copy.

## 2 · The negative control caught the fix, twice

**First round.** Written before believing anything: revert the pattern, confirm
the suite goes red.

It did not go red — **it went yellow**. `main()` reports every `ProbeError` as
exit 3, and `test_the_table_is_current…` *skips* on 3, correctly, because six of
the twenty-two artifacts live outside `engine-rig/` and a checkout without them
genuinely cannot run the check. A rendering fault is not that: it reproduces on
every checkout, and reporting it as "not checkable here" would have hidden the
fix the same way the original bug was hidden — the mistake D-030 names.

So the failure got its own type and its own exit code: `PlaceholderError` → rc 2,
and the test asserts `rc != 2` before it asserts `rc == 0`.

**Second round, and the first fix was not enough.** The adversarial pass ran the
control a third way — revert the pattern *and* hide one artifact — and the suite
went yellow again. `main()` probes before it renders, so `verify()` raised on the
missing artifact and returned 3 before the render was ever reached. The `rc != 2`
assertion only bit on checkouts where the skip branch was never going to fire.
The fix that reaches it is `render_selfcheck()`: substitute every known key with
a sentinel, ask only the question that needs no artifact — does every template
render, and is every key referenced a key that exists — and run it *before* the
first probe. Now pinned by its own test, which passes on a checkout with no
`runs/` directory at all.

Three negative controls, all re-run after the fix:

| control | before E13 | after |
|---|---|---|
| pristine | 0, pass | 0, pass |
| pattern reverted, all artifacts present | 0, **pass** (the bug) | 2, **fail** |
| pattern reverted, one artifact hidden | 3, **skip** | 2, **fail** |

`test_sub_refuses_a_key_its_own_matcher_cannot_see` now asserts
`PlaceholderError` rather than its parent, because the two carry different exit
codes and therefore different suite outcomes; a test that accepted either would
pass again the day somebody collapsed them back together.

## 3 · Five of the 174 numbers were quoted from prose, and one of them was wrong

Classifying every fact by what its probe reads:

| provenance | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a JSON/JSONL artifact | 62 | 71 |
| a text report or log inside a `runs/` directory | 107 | 108 |
| **narrative outside any run** | **5** | **1** |
| total facts | 174 | 180 |

*(This table read 68 / 108 in the first draft — a transposition that preserved
the total and so looked self-consistent. The adversarial pass recomputed both
columns from the two versions of `FACTS` and found 71 / 108: the diff adds seven
probes on `ladder.json`, one on a `logs/` file and one on `p13-fd-real`, and
removes none. In an item whose thesis is "a number quoted from a narrative is a
number nobody re-derived", the audit's own headline was a number nobody
re-derived. It is the most on-the-nose defect in this run and it was found by
somebody else.)*

The five: `fd.startup_ms`, `fd.search_share`, `fd.crossover`, `dl.m9_ringstuck`
(all `engine-rig/STATUS.md`) and `fd.never_fuzzed` (`fuzzlab/MUTATION.md`).

A regex against `STATUS.md` is a drift check that compares **prose to prose**.
It cannot fail while the narrative is self-consistent, however far the narrative
has drifted from the bench — and it had:

* **`fd.search_share` published `4.1 ms of a 181 ms bill`, and no artifact gives
  that row a 181 ms wall.** `ladder.json`'s `sokoban-far6` / `fd-optimal/lmcut`
  row is `search 4.1 ms, wall 187.3 ms`. The `4.1` was right and travelled with a
  wall time that was never measured for it. *(The first draft of this finding
  said "181 appears in no artifact", flatly. It does: E2's `RUN_STATE.md:38`
  publishes 181.8 for `gripper-08`/ipdb, and `wall - fd_total` for the far6/ipdb
  row is 181.2. Neither is the number in question, so the finding stands — but an
  absolute a `grep` refutes has no business in a document about numbers that do
  not survive a grep.)*
* **`dl.m9_ringstuck` published `44 → 22` from STATUS.md**, while
  `runs/p13-fd-real/dividend.json` has carried
  `stub_expansions_before: 44, stub_expansions_after: 22` all along. Right by
  luck, sourced by narrative.

Three of the four `STATUS.md` facts are now computed from the bench artifacts
(`ladder.json`, `p13-fd-real/dividend.json`); the fourth, `fd.startup_ms`
(`"140 and 260"`), has no successor — it was deleted rather than re-pointed,
because §4 below is what happened when it was measured. `fd.never_fuzzed` is the
one narrative fact left standing: it is the string `stub-bfs`, a label naming
which rung a code path forces, not a measurement.

**`STATUS.md` itself was corrected in the same pass.** Removing the probes would
otherwise have made things worse rather than better: the regex
`r"the search itself is (4\.1 ms of a 181 ms bill)"` was, for all its faults, the
only thing in the repository that would have broken if someone fixed that
sentence. Re-pointing the fact at `ladder.json` left the false sentence in place
and pinned by nothing at all. So the bullet now carries the probed numbers, says
which of them it used to get wrong, and records that it is downstream of
`ENGINE_TABLE.md` rather than a second source for it.

## 4 · Re-pointing at the bench refuted the sentence the numbers were in

The `fd_adapter` row said:

> FD's cost here is startup, not search — every FD row sits between **140 and
> 260 ms** almost regardless of instance, and on `sokoban-far6` the search is
> 4.1 ms of a 181 ms bill.

**The bench times three nested clocks, not two.** Every one of the 51 FD rungs
carries `search_seconds ⊆ fd_total_seconds ⊆ wall_seconds`, and E2's own
`RUN_STATE.md` says so. This run's first attempt at the correction read the
outer and inner clocks, never read the middle one, and published a cell asserting
that the bench "counts that as neither" — which the artifact refutes on its own
face. The adversarial pass caught it. The middle clock is not a detail: it is
exactly where the disputed time sits, and `wall − fd_total` is a **far** better
statement of the original claim than the wall-clock band ever was.

Computed over all 51 timed rungs:

| | |
|---|---|
| driver startup, `wall − fd_total` | **144.5 to 181.2 ms, median 154.9** |
| median FD wall clock | **163.3 ms** |
| median search share of that wall | **0.2 %** |
| widest search share | **502.9 ms of 666.2 (75.5 %)** on `gripper-10`/lmcut |
| slowest row | **1796.8 ms wall, 1615.6 inside FD, 0.2 in search** on `sokoban-far6`/ipdb |
| that row's pattern-database build, from its log | **1.621222 s** |

So the published band was wrong, but **not in both directions** — the first
draft of this finding said it was, and no row falls below 140 ms (the minimum
wall is 146.5). It fails upward, twice, for two different reasons. On
`gripper-10`/lmcut the search really does dominate, so "not search" is not
general. And on `sokoban-far6`/ipdb the wall clock is an order of magnitude above
the floor while search costs essentially nothing — that time is inside FD and
outside search, and
`runs/…-E2-fd-ladder-bench/logs/far6.fd-optimal-ipdb.base.log:103` attributes
1.621222 s of it to the hill-climbing pattern-collection generator. That
attribution had been prose in two places and is now a probed fact; the ~175 ms
between it and the 1796.8 is the driver floor, which the startup band accounts
for independently.

The row now states startup, the median, and both counterexamples, and every one
of those figures is computed from the bench. The claim that survives is narrower
and still the useful one: *on the typical instance, FD's bill is startup* — and
the crossover is at `gripper-08`, recomputed as the first gripper size where the
stub's wall clock exceeds the **fastest** optimal rung's, which is the comparison
that favours the stub least. The cell's old rider "above every instance this rig
generates" was false — `gripper-09` and `gripper-10` are both above it and one of
them is quoted two sentences earlier — and now says "above every instance the
*engines* generate, though the bench's own ladder runs past it", which is what
E2's `RUN_STATE.md` said correctly before the table paraphrased it.

## 5 · A run directory that disagrees with itself, left as a finding rather than fixed

Chasing the 181 turned up something bigger than the one number. E2's
hand-written `RUN_STATE.md` §1 timing table and its machine-generated
`LADDER.md` / `ladder.json` disagree on **every cell they share**:

| row | `RUN_STATE.md` §1 | `LADDER.md` / `ladder.json` |
|---|---|---|
| `far6` | 246.7 / 183.2 / 1774.1 / 182.9 | 253.9 / 187.3 / 1796.8 / 185.4 |
| `gripper-08` | 270.4 / 218.5 / 181.8 | 280.2 / 227.6 / 191.8 |
| `gripper-10` | 1953.9 / 692.5 / 263.1 | 1926.5 / 666.2 / 262.9 |

A systematic few-percent offset, consistent with a different **execution** of the
bench rather than a different repeat — `ladder.json` stores one timing per rung
(`repeats: 3`, `repeat_rule: "fastest of N"`) and no per-repeat data, so "a
different repeat" is not something any artifact supports, and this run's first
draft asserted it in a subordinate clause. Recorded here, not repaired: fixing it
means deciding which execution E2's narrative describes, which is E2's to answer
and needs its own item. What matters for this table is that **no fact reads
`RUN_STATE.md`**, so the drift is contained to that run's prose.

## 6 · The table's own provenance claim was too strong

The header said *"every number here is probed out of an artifact under `runs/`"*
and the provenance section said *"a number that could not be pointed back at a
run does not appear in the table"*. **Twelve of the 180 facts point at no run**:
four at `engine-rig/artifacts/candidates.jsonl`, seven at `fuzzlab/out/`, one at
`fuzzlab/MUTATION.md`. Those are standing artifacts rather than the record of one
run, which is defensible — but the file asserted something else twice, and the
work order asked specifically for traceability to `runs/`. Both sentences now
say what is true and give the split (`168 of 180`).

The footer had the matching problem in the other direction: *"Runs referenced:"*
was a hand-written list of six runs, and it **omitted E17** — which supplies 31
facts, second only to E11's 87. It was written before E17 landed and nothing made
it wrong. It is now generated from the probes, with a count per source, so a new
source cannot go unmentioned. The count that falls out of it is itself worth
reading: **87 of 180 facts come from E11**, whose harnesses are explicitly not
committed.

## What this run did not do

* **No new experiments**, as the work order required. Every number added here was
  already inside `ladder.json` or `dividend.json` and had simply never been read
  by the generator.
* **It did not re-derive the E11 partials.** 108 of the 180 facts are regexes
  into text reports under `runs/`, and **87 of them are E11's**, whose harnesses
  are explicitly not committed ("the harness lives in the session scratchpad").
  That is weaker provenance than a JSON artifact and it is the largest remaining
  structural weakness in the table's numbers — half the table rests on one run
  that cannot be re-executed from this repository. Re-deriving it is E11's work
  run again, not a table audit, and it needs its own item.
* **It corrected only the `fd_adapter` bullet of `STATUS.md`**, which is the one
  the table used to be downstream of. `STATUS.md` carries other figures E9 and
  E17 already recorded as stale — the forgery catalogue's 25/24 against E5's
  31/2, and two different suite counts — and this run left them alone rather than
  widen its scope into a general narrative sweep.
* **It did not change any engine.** Zero bytes changed under `engines/`.
